Project Description: This project explores local queer history in Northern Virginia. It began as a class project in the Fall 2023 as a digital walking tour exploring sites of queer history in Alexandria, VA, with ArcGIS Storymaps. The project received support from the Alexandria Historical Society and the Roy Rosenzweig Center for History and New Media to expand inquiry into Northern Virginia.
We are currently researching and building a website for the expanded content.
Collaborators: Hannah LeComte, Alexandra Miller, and Ashleigh Williams
Link: https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/c1bf986aba7a43cd8811e03591414a66

content:
About Me I am a PhD student in History at George Mason University. As a graduate research assistant at the Roy Rosenzweig Center for History and New Media, I do web development and data visualization for data-driven and digital public history projects. My broad research interests are 20th century United States, war and society, and digital history. I am currently researching the local queer history of Northern Virginia, and recreation opporunities for military personnel and their families with the transition to the all-volunteer force.
I am originally from Salisbury, MD, and received my BA in History from Bridgewater College. When not doing history, I enjoy golfing, reading (fiction!), and supporting women’s sports.
Find Me George Mason University LinkedIn Github Observable Contact Me Email: sscott35@gmu.edu
